title: Behavioral & HR Rounds
scope_in: Behavioral interview rounds: STAR stories, competencies (ownership, conflict, failure, ambiguity, leadership, influence), 'tell me about yourself', motivation, questions for the interviewer.
scope_out: Technical correctness (other domains), salary negotiation scripts (separate domain if wanted).

modes.output: interviewer questions one at a time with realistic follow-ups, graded at the end
shape it into a STAR story: gaps flagged, questions to extract metrics; saved to the story bank
a single question, rapid scoring, sharper rewrite of the weakest sentence
re-test saved stories against new questions to check they flex across competencies

ladder: Simple prompts: tell me about yourself, why this company, a strength.
Standard STAR: a conflict, a deadline you met, a time you learned something.
Probing: failure with real consequences, disagreeing with a manager, ambiguity, with 2 follow-ups.
Senior-level: influence without authority, a decision with incomplete data, org-level impact, trade-offs between people and delivery.
Hostile/ambiguous interviewer: challenges your claims, asks 'what would you do differently?', probes ownership vs team credit.

flaws.F-NO-METRIC: No numbers or concrete evidence of impact.
flaws.F-GENERIC: Could be anyone's answer; no specifics.
flaws.F-WEAK-SITUATION: Low-stakes situation chosen for the competency.

x_fields.story_ref: Story-bank id of the story used.
x_fields.quantified: true/false: a metric in the result.

items_note: the user's story text (the story bank) and the rewritten version
rubric_body:
Score each 0-2:

| Dimension | Looks for |
|-----------|-----------|
| Structure | S/T/A/R clearly delineated, answer first-pass under ~2.5 min |
| Ownership | specific personal actions ('I decided...'), team credit stated accurately |
| Impact | measurable result, scale, stakes |
| Reflection | learning, what would change |
| Relevance | story fits the competency asked |
| Handling follow-ups | consistent, honest, non-defensive |
gate_extra: Never invent or embellish the user's experiences. Stories come only from the user; you coach structure, extract specifics, and rewrite their own words more sharply.
Do not 'grade' honesty away: if a claim sounds implausible, probe it as an interviewer would instead of silently accepting it.
loop_extra:
### Behavioral specifics
`story` mode: ask at most 3 extraction questions at a time (what exactly did YOU do, what was the number, what would you change); then produce the STAR draft in the user's voice and `save-item` it as the story bank entry (item.ref `beh-<competency>-<slug>`). `mock`: one question, wait for the answer, one follow-up, move on.
